title: Beansy's son and a failed attempt to book the band again
summary: After giving up his band, Albert let Beansy's son finance and book it; the venture failed and Albert rebooked it himself.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So you've had a couple of breaks in there. That's right. I see. You know, I never did get your boy's name Chauncey Highland. Chauncey Highland. How do you spell it? Biggest crook you've ever seen. S-Y-L-E-N-D. H?
Y-L-E-N-D. Yeah. I'd never seen his name written on him. I didn't know how to spell it on him. Right. Well, he confidants Beansy.
I had given up my band in New Orleans. That was the first time. And he confidants Beansy in backing me. Beansy had a son that he wanted to put in business.

So Beansy called me. Beansy and I have been great friends. I told him and I want to sell him out and you probably couldn't help him. I don't want the money, he says I just want him to learn the business. So he financed the deal for about $5,000 and bought this crook of automobile and he got on the road to book the band. He hadn't gotten as far as Austin when he had messed up about five or six days. But I organized my band again. That's when I got Lionel Reason in the band.
